children: Tesla (TSLA) and SpaceX are in early merger talks; independent special committees assess a possible deal, Musk excluded from committee; no terms set; TSLA shares rose ~1–2% in after-hours trading.
Tesla (TSLA) began commercial Cybercab robotaxi ops in Austin with ~350 registered, ~187 active. Supervised/limited autonomous rides run in six U.S. cities; Phoenix testing approval secured.
Tesla (TSLA) reports Q3 earnings Oct 21. Street expects $0.44 EPS and $28.3B revenue — EPS down ~12% year‑over‑year, revenue roughly flat vs. prior-year quarter.
ARK updated its TSLA model with 2031 targets: base $4,400, bull $5,000, bear $3,300. Projects ~10.2M deliveries, ~$1.45T revenue, ~80% value from Robotaxi, ~8–10M robotaxi units.
Tesla (TSLA) delivered 486,532 vehicles and deployed 13.7 GWh of energy storage. Stock trades ~10.8% above a $336.57 GF value. Traders note margins, energy profitability and autonomy costs.
Tesla (TSLA) CFO says capex will rise over 2–3 years to fund robotaxis, Optimus and infrastructure; company arranging large funding, including a reported $30 billion credit facility.
Analysts modeled a potential Tesla (TSLA)–SpaceX merger by 2031, projecting combined revenue ~$3.8 trillion and EBIT ~$2.7 trillion, with SpaceX supplying most sales and profit and joint tech plans.
Ahead of Tesla (TSLA) Q3 results Oct 21: near-term put/call 0.47, rising call volume, top weekly strike ~$397 (~6% upside). Stock trading above key moving averages; RSI near mid-50s.
Traders link Tesla (TSLA) valuation to its AI and self‑driving progress more than EV sales; investors expect management comments on AI after Tesla’s October 21 results to move the stock.
Tesla (TSLA) held 11,509 BTC as of June 30, making its corporate Bitcoin holding notable among public firms when compared with other reported corporate treasuries.
